findings:
🔵 [r1-skip-to-fail-scope] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The hunk in assert_r1_nosetsid_with_jobcontrol_still_enforces converts a host-dependent SKIP into a hard fail; this is outside the "append to the suite" scope and could turn the suite red on a host where job control does not isolate the worker pgid. Not blocking: bash set -m reliably gives background jobs their own pgid, and the Verify run on this host passed. Consider restoring the SKIP or asserting only when a pgid was observed.
🔵 [cgroup-alive-superset] CUT/FOLLOW-UP _watchdog_worker_alive in the SCOPE_UNIT branch also consults WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID after the WORKER_RP zombie/missing check; the spec asked only for the rp state. Harmless superset (a zombie rp is also the only member of that pgid), no change required.
🔵 [stamp-then-unstamp-ordering] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The fired marker is created before the TERM send and removed on a non-zero return, rather than created strictly after delivery. Net observable behavior matches the spec (marker persists only when delivery was reported, and the parent's wait can only return in that window if the worker already exited, in which case the group kill on the zombie group succeeds anyway), so this is an ordering choice with a justified race comment, not a defect.
